newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos portworkers approve 24-hour workday plan.
newsitem.headline: Santos portworkers approve 24-hour workday plan.

text.p: Portworker representatives at the Brazilian port of Santos have approved a proposal to allow the port to function 24 hours a day, seven days a week, port authority Codesp said.
The plan would initially be implemented in the Tecon container terminal on an experimental basis, Codesp said in a statement.

"Representatives of workers and port operators...consider the inititiave vital for the increase in the movement of cargoes through the port of Santos, as well as allowing a rise in productivity and the maintenance of jobs and average wages," it said.
The Tecon terminal would work 362 days a year under the new system, shutting for Christmas, New Year and Labor Day.

The port authority and unions still had to agree on a reduction in tariffs and wages for nightshifts, among other issues. Codesp was due to present a proposal on extending the 24-hour workday to other areas of port activity like customs, railways and sanitary supervision.
Santos will continue to operate during the carnival holiday between Feb 10 and 12, Codesp said in a separate statement.
